correctness.rationale: Conditioning the first A coupon to be the fixed starting vertex changes no total-time distribution by exchangeability and leaves independent future draws. Thus the side must be B precisely when T_b>=T_a: compare physical step indices 2T_b-1 and 2(T_a-1), including a=1. Summing the finite inclusion-exclusion expressions for the A point mass and B survival function over time gives the stated denominator by a geometric series; zero bases at time zero represent 1. Within each non-start orbit, exchangeability gives the claimed probabilities. For m>=2 the squared l2 norm of a mixture of translates of the last geometric stage is at most the squared norm 1/(2m-1) of that stage alone. It is strict for m>=3 because the earlier-stage sum has nondegenerate support, and two distinct translates differ. For the collision asymptotic use integer Fourier inversion after t rescaling: one geometric factor gives a uniform (1+2t^2/pi^2)^{-1} bound on |t|<=pi*m. Gumbel convergence, independent limits, dominated convergence and Plancherel yield the integral of the Gumbel density squared, 1/4. The deterministic difference of centerings divided by m is delta*log(m)/m+o(1) for delta=o(m); centered fluctuation differences are tight, and at finite limits their independent Gumbel difference is continuous logistic. The two-vertex case uses the pgf at 1/2 of the other coupon time and yields the central-binomial identity. Verified 81 small side probabilities, 20 thin-part instances, and 11 balanced cases exactly with a separately written state recurrence (python3 /workspace/branches/frozen_math_recheck.py 5); asymptotic claims use the argument, not those cases. The frozen checker was inspected, not executed.
